correctness.rationale: For undirected adjacency, the antitone graph-NOR support map A->V\N(A) has A subset F^2(A), hence F^3=F. Every state reaches recurrence after one update. A full cases proof for supports in a graph join shows only factor-supported periodic states, except the universal empty/full orbit; an orbit involving the empty state in a factor occurs exactly for isolate-free factors. This establishes Q correction and fixed-point additivity. Counting cross-factor nonempty subsets plus factor total-dominating sets establishes the exact universal basin. The K_m closed formulas include the one-vertex exception. Direct exhaustive bit-mask tests pass for 5,625 ordered labelled graph pairs of orders 1..4 and 120 larger deterministic-seed pairs; these do not stand in place of the all-graph proof.

originality.rationale: The join-specific formulas for primitive two-cycles, isolate corrections, and universal basin volumes were not found in the inspected earlier literature or accessible statement archive. Positive conjunctive dynamics (2008), AND-NOT fixed-point enumeration (2011), and self-inclusive NOR/maxterm systems (2017, 2020) neither match the open-neighborhood model nor imply the combined join formulas. The published Rule 5 iterate formula treats a ring only. Prior coverage remains possible in inaccessible or unindexed materials and this is not an independence or priority certificate.

Complete historical text for the 2011 AND-NOT and 2018 maxterm/minterm papers was not accessible; only the confirmed different scope of inspected portions and later descriptions were used.
The 2008 positive-operator theory and 2023 Rule 5 special case show broad mathematical background, so no claim of inventing antitone polarity or fixed-point correspondence is made.

value.rationale: Graph joins are canonical and the theorem computes natural complete recurrent orbit statistics and a distinguished entire basin for arbitrary factor graphs. The isolated-vertex threshold is sharp. When a clique is adjoined, the oscillatory orbit count stays invariant or gains one even as the number of initial configurations outside a single two-cycle basin grows only linearly in clique size, despite an exponential global state space. This broad structural separation of attractor number and accessibility is neither a small numeric improvement nor a restatement of only the maximal-independent-set fixed-point theorem.
